label: R Draconis
position_source: SIMBAD (simbad.harvard.edu) V* R Dra, moved to 2026.0

scale.method: asinh: grey = asinh(t/0.002) / asinh(1/0.002), t = (value - vmin)/(vmax - vmin); vmin = 1.0 percentile, vmax = brightest good pixel of all frames (same scale for every frame). Faint parts are brightened, so grey levels are not proportional to brightness

method: up to 8 exposures per visit (closest to the visit's mean time), each IMAGE - ZODI with the official flag mask, reprojected onto this grid and added up with 1/variance weights
notes: R Draconis is so bright that its centre is saturated in every exposure (in single exposures, no value up to 6 pixels from the centre). The add-up fills part of that hole from the exposures where those pixels were not saturated, which is why very bright pixels ring the striped centre.
These frames use an asinh brightness scale so that the faint halo shows next to the core: grey levels are not proportional to brightness, but every visit uses the same scale.

No light curve: the light around the saturated core could only be measured from 7 pixels out, and only rings up to 3 pixels out were checked to follow a star's brightness. So these frames do not show how much R Draconis changed; its pulsation was not checked here.
